site_or_subject: Johor Data Centre Development Coordination Committee approvals, rejections and Tier 1/2 halt
operator: Johor State Government (DCDCC; Special Technical Committee)
record: Johor's committee began vetting applications in June 2024 and, per its vice-chairman Lee Ting Han (Nov 2024), rejected nearly 30% of applications in five months (4 of 14 foreign-operator bids), citing failure to show sustainable water/energy practices and sites lacking utility infrastructure; Johor capacity was stated at 10 MW (2021), ~1.3 GW (Nov 2024), 2.7 GW projected 2027. In Nov 2025 state exco Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said 51 projects were approved (17 operational, 11 under construction, 23 unbuilt) and the state 'will no longer approve' Tier 1 and Tier 2 facilities, which can use up to 50 million litres/day versus ~200,000 L/day for Tier 3/4; data centres needing water must use reclaimed water rather than Syarikat Air Johor supply. In Jan 2026 the state set a WUE threshold of 1.8.

gap: Approved-project counts (42 as of Q2 2025; 51 as of Nov 2025) and MW figures (1.3 GW vs an unreconciled 1.6 GW cited by ISEAS) are not published in a single state register; no primary committee documents are public.

record: NSW Planning confirmed to Reuters (Sep 2025) that all 10 data-centre applications ruled on since 2021 were approved (A$6.6bn), projecting up to 9.6 GL/yr of potable water (~2% of Sydney's maximum supply); Sydney Water projected data centres could use up to 135 GL (a quarter of available water) by 2035.
